decisive_items: Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli in distal main pulmonary arteries extending into lobar and segmental branches of upper and lower lobes bilaterally
Dilated right ventricle with RV-LV ratio >1.5
response.rationale: CT angiogram directly demonstrates acute pulmonary emboli, the definitive cause of the presentation. Elevated D-dimer and RV strain support this. R5 and R6 describe downstream effects of PE, not the primary diagnosis. R2 is contradicted by normal ECG.

rejected.why: Right ventricular failure is a consequence of PE, not the most likely primary diagnosis.
Cor pulmonale is a chronic complication; acute PE is the underlying cause.
ECG shows no ischemia, and troponin elevation is explained by PE-related strain.
